# Ho-Smart v0.1.1 — Initial local receiver field-test integration

**Focus:** Establish verified local communication and detailed diagnostics for the Ho-Smart HS006W driveway-alarm receiver.

## Why this release was developed

This was an early field-test build aimed at understanding what the HS006W receiver actually exposes over its local ESP RainMaker Security1 connection. Its primary goal was to collect reliable real-world data before treating receiver status values as proven driveway alarms.

## What changed

- Added local receiver onboarding using the Ho-Smart account to discover the per-device Proof of Possession (POP); the account password is not stored by the integration.
- Implemented local Security1 communication with the HS006W at its verified local-control port.
- Exposed receiver power, battery, volume, channel, and armed-state entities.
- Added high-frequency development polling, a passive UDP listener, and persistent redacted debug/event journals for field testing.
- Captured raw receiver event, channel, and channel-name values without assuming they represented actual motion.

## Limitations and testing

**Early field-test build, not a proven driveway-alarm delivery solution.** The original local receiver protocol investigation had not established a reliable local stream of actual driveway alarms. Later releases introduced cloud alarm-history support after field diagnostics showed that local status was insufficient.

## Installation

Install through HACS as a custom integration and restart Home Assistant. Later versions provide more complete alarm handling and should be preferred for current deployments.
